newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee see-saws on exchange move on rules.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee see-saws on exchange move on rules.

text.p: Robusta coffee futures see-sawed but still ended broadly higher on roaster buying, gains in New York and worries over the threat of Mexican frost, traders said.
But the main unsettling factor was a surprise announcement from the exchange on validity of coffee grading certificates following changes, announced in March, on the way robusta coffee is graded.
The validity of grading certificates and transitional arrangement for grading come into effect from today, LIFFE said.
"This came out of the blue," said one trader."
"A lot of people started to move their positions around," he said. "It made a lot of difference to May/July which was trading at $15 premium and quickly went into discount because of that."

In the circular, LIFFE said grading certificates that have been issued and will continue to be issued against the current grading criteria will be valid for coffee tendered for delivery for January, March and May 1997 contracts only.

Coffee that is tendered for delivery against July 1997 and subsequent delivery months must have been graded against, and be accompanied by a valid grading certificate issued against the amended criteria.
By the close, most-active March was $2 up at $1,260 a tonne after trading betweem $1,262 and $1,246.

Elsewhere, traders said there was some trade selling and origin buying underneath the market. Sentiment was also helped by gains in New York and on forecasts of possible frost in the Mexican coffee belt on Thursday and Friday. "Frost is mostly likely on Thursday and Friday morning," broker GNI said.
"Mexico has suffered from frost before, alhtough the total quantity of coffee produced is around a fifth of that in Brazil," it said. "Veracruz, Puebla and Guerrero are the most vulnerable regions."
"However even the loss of half a million bags of coffee would be significant in the current market," the brokerage said.
